result:
I fixed the regression: in `anthrouter/http_util.py:120` the requests-remaining header name had lost an "s". It read `anthropic-ratelimit-request-remaining`, but the header the upstream actually sends is `anthropic-ratelimit-requests-remaining`. Because of the typo, the requests-remaining value was never captured, so it was stored as `None` and left out of the status report.

That one change fixed 3 of the 6 failing tests:
- `test_status_reports_the_last_rate_limit_window`
- `test_successful_request_records_usage_and_the_rate_limit_window`
- `test_admin_requests_reflects_a_dispatched_request`

I re-ran the three affected test files (`test_handlers.py`, `test_admin.py`, `test_config.py`), not the full suite: 264 passed, 3 failed. I didn't touch those 3 failures because they have nothing to do with rate limits:
- `test_cached_tier_is_not_replayed_into_a_different_requested_tier` and `test_locked_baseline_scopes_the_tier_slot_by_the_lock` expect routing reason `session_cached_tier` but get `classifier_rules_trivial`.
- `test_editable_fields_live_editable_fields` fails because the live-editable fields include an extra one, `oauth_usage_poll_interval`.
